item.title: Dynasty continues: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake wins 24th straight Section 2 girls' volleyball title
item.description: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Bethlehem for the Section 2, Class AA title on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - For 23 consecutive seasons, Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake girls' volleyball coach Gary Bynon watched his players rush each other on the court and celebrate capturing a Section 2 title. On Friday evening, Bynon looked on for a 24th time in as many seasons as his top-seeded Spartans swept No. 2 Bethlehem, 25-20, 25-16, 25-13, to claim the Class AA title at Saratoga Springs High School. "These are young kids," Bynon said. "Every team has their own championship. I told them today that before we went out. I said, ‘Listen, we're not here to repeat history. We're here to make it,' because this is theirs. It's not mine." Burnt Hills, ranked third in the state Class AA poll, captured its 31st championship overall. "This group is such an amazing team together," Burnt Hills junior outside hitter Alex Wemyss said. "I've never felt so close to a team in my life I don't think. We're all just best friends. We're all so young and I think we're all still developing. Every practice, every game, we're just getting better." Burnt Hills junior setter Leah Vaughan delivered 33 assists, and eighth grader Ella Tassone added 13 kills and five digs. Bethlehem senior setter Mae Walston provided 18 assists and sophomore Madelyn Palmer totaled seven kills. Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake celebrates after beating Bethlehem for the Section 2, Class AA title on Friday, Nov. 6, in Saratoga, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) Key moment Burnt Hills trailed by five points on three separate occasions in the opening set. Facing an 18-13 deficit, the Spartans used an 8-0 run to regain control. Wemyss totaled seven service points in the spurt and served up a blistering ace to level the set, 18-18. "It's so exciting being on this court and being in this gym with all these people," Wemyss said. "I think it's so great to come back from that with a team like this, especially in the sectionals, because (Bethlehem) is so amazing." "You can't make up five points in one serve, but you've got to score that one and then you've got to score another one," Bynon added. I thought that (Wemyss') big serves gave us that momentum. (Bethlehem is) such a good team and for us to be able to do that was a great thing." Star of the game Wemyss has been tremendous all season for Burnt Hills, but she played a crucial role in the Spartans weathering the storm in the first set as well as the remainder of the match. Wemyss finished Friday's match with 16 kills, nine digs, and four aces. "I think she's one of the top six rotation (outside hitters) in this area," Bynon said. "You can see she's a competitor. item.description: SHELBY — The Shelby Whippets fumbled on the very first play, but from then on, it was perfection. The slight hiccup was quickly erased as they cruised to a 42-3 Division IV Region 14 quarterfinal victory over Firelands on Friday, Nov. 6 and will host Perkins (11-0) on Nov. 13 in the regional semifinals. The Whippets were efficient in ever sense of the word on offense scoring 14 points in the first quarter and 21 in the second to build a 35-3 lead at the half and start the second half with a running clock. ONTARIO WINS: Ontario finds a way to win in regional quarterfinal victory over Columbian Michael Shepherd hit Brady Bowman for a 47-yard touchdown to open the scoring before Shepherd added a 1-yard TD run to close out the first quarter. Gavin Baker added a 1-yard TD run, Casyn Koch caught a 15-yard touchdown from Shepherd and Baker added his second TD of the night from five yards out all in the second quarter to build the insurmountable advantage. Shepherd added an 11-yard TD run in the third quarter for good measure. “Other than the fumble on the first play, I thought we were pretty dang efficient,” Shelby coach Rob Mahaney told Marc Hartz of the Shelby Daily Globe. “That is what we want to be. There will be games where we throw for 400 or run for 400, but we want to pride ourselves to take what the defense gives us and our kids did a great job of that tonight. We sustained drives and that will be huge for us next week against Perkins.” The Whippets (11-0) ran for 237 yards on 25 carries led by Baker’s 115-yard, 2-touchdown performance. Like Blevins added 49 yards while Brady Bowman had 44 and Shepherd had 31 with a pair of scores. “If we are going to do well in the postseason, it is going to fall on those guys up front,” Mahaney said. “Those senior offensive linemen did a great job for us tonight and Michael (Shepherd) was great in the read game. item.description: Holy Cross' Dae'Sean Graves (1) during their game against Ansonia Friday, October 9, 2026 at Municipal Stadium in Waterbury, Conn. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) BEACON FALLS - Dae'Sean Graves broke Connecticut's career receptions record Friday night as Holy Cross scored 38 unanswered second-half points to beat Woodland 38-14 in an NVL football game. Graves entered with 221 career catches, five shy of tying East Catholic's Joey Montalvo's mark of 226. He finished with seven catches for 110 yards and 228 for his career. On Oct. 23, the UConn commit also broke the state career record for touchdown receptions , surpassing Southington's Alex Jamele's mark of 50. Graves caught a touchdown pass as he broke the state's all-time reception record and led Holy Cross to a 38-14 victory over Woodland #cthsfb #connecticut #highschoolfootball (Kevin Roberts/Hearst Connecticut Media) The public address announcer noted Graves' achievement Friday, but Graves was already focused on the next play. "It was definitely good. At the time, I was really focused on the game," Graves said. "That just came, but I wasn't really focused on it. I really was focused on finishing the game. That was my thought process on it, on the announcement of it." Holy Cross was held scoreless in the first half at Woodland High School, where dense fog made a foghorn an easy substitute for an official's whistle. The Crusaders improved to 7-1 and held onto the No. 2 spot in the Class MM playoff standings behind St. Joseph, which was ranked No. 2 in the latest GametimeCT Top 10 poll . The Hawks fell to 5-3. Woodland used a single-wing style offense it installed a couple of weeks ago to build its 14-0 halftime lead. Justin Pringle finished off an 18-play, 86-yard drive with a 2-yard touchdown. item.title: ‘Gyro Greek brain’ – Kobe Bryant’s ex-teammate brutally calls Giannis Antetokounmpo dumb
item.description: Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Miami Heat may be struggling, but one former Laker has made some truly out of pocket comments about the Greek Freak. The move from Milwaukee to Miami isn’t going exactly how he planned it for Giannis Antetokounmpo at the moment. The new-look Heat have started the season 3-6, and recently lost against the Golden State Warriors. The Greek Freak has been in the headlines as a result, and received his share of criticism. Doc Rivers recently suggested that Giannis is hard to coach, for example. His style of play has been called into question by some. It is worth noting that despite this, he is averaging 27.3 points, 12.7 rebounds, and 5.6 assists per game. And now, one former Laker may have gone overboard with his comments. Nick Young makes out of pocket comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo’s offensive game Former NBA players on podcasts are some of the most viral commentators when it comes to the modern game. The Gil’s Arena podcast, in particular, is known for some fairly wild takes at times. Nick Young, who is a regular voice on the show, recently made some truly provocative comments about Antetokounmpo. Speaking about Giannis’ offensive game, Kobe Bryant’s former teammate simply ended up insulting the two-time NBA MVP. The n**** dumb. That’s all. He just Gyro Greek brain. All he learned was to go coast to coast. That n**** ain’t changed. I haven’t seen a jump shot,” Young said. “He been going coast to coast since he came in the league. ‘Aye, set a screen?’ ‘Nah, I’m gonna go coast-to-coast. That’s what I do.’ “If they keep losing… That coach in Miami, they ain’t going to treat him like they did Doc. If they keep losing and he go coast to coast…” These comments from Young are unlikely to be received well by Giannis or his fans. While there can be some criticisms of his game, this is well beyond what would be considered normal. It remains to be seen if the Heat superstar will respond to this.

item.title: Unioto, Piketon reach end of season with Week 12 losses
item.description: Bellbrook 49, Unioto 14 Bellbrook took care of business against Unioto (8-4) on Nov. 6 in a Division III Region 12 quarterfinal by a 49-14 final. Bellbrook's Kenton Gerdes started the scoring with a 24-yard touchdown run, and while the Shermans drove the ball down the field when it was their turn, Jack Kosins intercepted the ball at the 1-yard line. The Golden Eagles then drove the ball 96 yards, capped this time by a 14-yard Bronson Epifano run to make it 14-0. JC Penewit caught the next score on a three-yard pass from Grant Diorio, making it 21-0. Unioto got on the board when Blake Braden hit Brayden Harsha for a 37-yard score. Diorio, though, made it 28-7 at the half when he ran one in behind a bevy of blockers. Unioto didn’t go quietly, as the combo and Braden and Harsha hooked up again, this time from 32 yards out to make it 28-14. But Grant Diorio answered with his third score on a one-yard run to make it 35-14 with 6:30 left in the third. Kosins picked off his second pass of the game on the next possession and the Golden Eagles cashed that in when Kosins scored on a 19-yard run to make it 42-14. Bellbrook picked up a fumble on the ensuing kickoff and turned that into more points on the next play on Epifano’s second score to round out the night's final score and put an end to Unioto's season. Bellbrook (11-0) will host Miami Trace, who topped Chillicothe, on Nov. 13 in a Division III, Region 12 semifinal. Fort Frye 37, Piketon 0 After a thrilling 14-13 win over Meigs to start its postseason run, Piketon (7-5) fell to Fort Frye (10-1) in a Division V, Region 19 quarterfinal on Friday, Nov. 6. The postseason appearance marks the Redstreaks' second straight playoff berth and seventh in school history. item.title: Rutgers overcomes early air balls to blow out New Haven, secure first win for acting head coach Brandin Knight
item.description: After watching his Scarlet Knights launch multiple air balls in the opening minutes of his first regular season game as acting head coach, Brandin Knight winced. Rutgers was also allowing New Haven to knock down 3-pointers and secure offensive rebounds that led to second-chance points. But with just over a minute remaining in the first half, Rutgers sprung to life when point guard Tariq Francis threw an alley-oop pass to backcourt mate Jamichael Davis, who finished it with flair. Next time down, Davis, a 6-foot-2 senior, hit a 3-pointer; the home crowd erupted. “Unbelievable,” Knight said. “Unbelievable. I don’t know what ladder he stepped on.” That flourish put Rutgers up 15 points, and the lead ballooned to 30 points midway through the second half. The sequence proved to be the most important in Rutgers’ 81-54 victory. With head coach Steve Pikiell absent due to his ongoing battle with cancer, Knight secured his first win with a roster that remains in transition and in need for repetitions together. “Just thankful and grateful that everyone showed up,” Knight said. “It felt electric for the first night. My happiness comes in how we do as a team.” Rutgers, which finished last season 14-20, will play NJIT at home on Tuesday. item.title: Report: Judge's ruling could make Bellarmine eligible for CCS football playoffs
item.description: Bellarmine defeated Menlo-Atherton 30-7 in 2022, the last time the Bells were in the CCS playoffs. They had clinched a berth to return this year until Monday's news that they had to forfeit all their wins. (Courtesy of Dennis Lee) Bellarmine's football playoff season is still alive. At least temporarily. According to the San Jose Mercury News, a Santa Clara County judge issued a temporary restraining order against the Central Coast Section, which on Monday ruled the Bells would have to forfeit their six wins this season for using an ineligible player. The CCS ruling could not be appealed according to section officials, so Bellarmine, as principal Rod Jemison promised, went to court. Superior Court Judge Panteha E. Saban rendered the TRO on Friday, with another hearing scheduled for Thursday, the Mercury News reported. The problem with that is that the CCS starts its playoffs next week and plans to announce those pairings are scheduled for Sunday. Bellarmine (6-3, 3-3 West Catholic Athletic League) closes its regular season Saturday at Riordan. Using a point system and MaxPreps computer rankings, the Bells are likely to be seeded in the bottom half of the CCS Division 1 bracket, the most competitive of the five divisions. If the forfeits stand, the Bells will be 0-9 and couldn't qualify for the CCS playoffs, even with a win at Riordan. But because of the judge's order, Bellarmine would likely be back in unless the CCS delays its pairings to Thursday, which is highly unlikely. Messages to CCS Commissioner Dave Grissom were not immediately answered. Nor were they earlier in the week when the announcement of Bellarmine's forfeits was made. In a letter to parents attained by the Chronicle this week, Jemison wrote: "We do not dispute the violation occurred. However, we disagree with the severity of the associated consequences and their impact on the entire team. "Bellarmine received notice of a violation of CIF Central Coast Section (CCS) by-laws regarding athletic eligibility for transfer students. The CCS Commissioner outlined consequences for the violation, including athletic ineligibility for the student-athlete in question and retroactive forfeiture of games in which that student participated. "We acknowledge it is Bellarmine's responsibility to ensure compliance and understanding of CIF and CCS regulations, and we are committed to identifying and addressing any gaps in our oversight." A judge reportedly agreed that the punishment might have been too great and wants to discuss the issues. If the CCS seeds Bellarmine into the Division 1 playoffs, then the court rules the forfeits were justisfied, what the section will do then will be of note. One possibility is that the team scheduled to play the Bells would receive a first-round bye. Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Fossil Ridge football season ends with playoff road loss
item.description: The Fossil Ridge High School football season ended in the Colorado Class 5A playoffs for a fifth time in six seasons. No. 12 Regis Jesuit routed No. 21 Fossil 49-21 in the 5A first round Nov. 6 at Kellogg Stadium in Aurora. The Raiders scored on their first five possessions and led 35-0 before Fossil got on the board late in the first half. Heralded junior quarterback Luke Rubley threw five touchdowns, two to Colt Jones. That sparked a Regis offense which had faced tough sledding against top teams like Grandview and Valor Christians to close the regular season. Regis moves on for a rematch against No. 5 Grandview in the 5A second round Nov. 13. The Raiders are now 4-0 all-time against the SaberCats, with all four wins coming since 2022. Fossil Ridge couldn't get anything going until it was too late against a Denver-area power. Fossil quarterback Colton Jantz capped off another strong campaign, throwing TD passes to Caleb Camping and fellow junior Gavin Zanotelli . Zanotelli caught another touchdown from running back Will Hough off a trick play to open the second half. Even after Fossil forced an ensuing fumble, the momentum was short-lived. Regis Jesuit's Andrew Mihm intercepted Jantz and returned it for a pick-six score. It was a disappointing exit for Fossil after showcasing major improvement in October. Fossil Ridge won four of its last five regular season games following a 1-4 start, beating rival Rocky Mountain, upsetting Legacy and pushing unbeaten Fort Collins to the wire before defeating Erie and Rock Canyon to return to .500. This was still a bounce back season for the SaberCats, who went 2-8 last year while missing the 5A playoffs for the first time since 2020. With Jantz and top target Zanotelli headlining the likely returners next season, Fossil could make some more noise in 2027. item.title: New Champion Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris Trade Blows in Sao Paulo GP Friday Practice
item.description: Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris were the top two drivers in Sao Paulo GP Friday Practice. (Source: MEGA) The newly crowned 2026 F1 champion Kimi Antonelli and the outgoing champion Lando Norris traded top spots during Friday practice sessions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Antonelli, who became the youngest-ever F1 champion at the Mexican Grand Prix last weekend, finished second in FP1 before bouncing back to top the timesheets in FP2. Norris, meanwhile, made an encouraging start to the weekend as he led the opening practice session. View this post on Instagram Both the drivers emerged as the leading contenders, showing impressive pace throughout the Friday practice. Red Bull Racing driver Max Verstappen also showed encouraging speed at Interlagos. Lando Norris Edges Kimi Antonelli in FP1 Lando Norris led FP1 in Brazil. (Source: MEGA) The McLaren driver began the Sao Paulo Grand Prix weekend by setting the benchmark in FP1, recording a fastest lap of 1:11.717, ahead of Antonelli. The Mercedes driver finished 0.082 seconds behind Norris. Verstappen was the third-fastest in the opening session. The seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton was fourth for Ferrari with a 1:12.041, while Mercedes' George Russell finished fifth with a lap time of 1:12.103. FP1 also featured several rookie appearances, as six regular drivers stepped aside for their teams to fulfil the mandatory young-driver practice requirement. Out of the six test drivers, Gabriele Mini was the fastest as he finished seventh ahead of McLaren's Leonardo Fornaroli in 11 th . Antonelli initially established himself at the front on medium tires before improving his time. However, he struggled slightly during his first soft-tire attempt, locking up and running wide at Turn 1. Norris, on soft tyres, took the opportunity to move ahead and stayed at the top until the chequered flag. Kimi Antonelli Bounced Back in FP2 Kimi Antonelli edged out Lando Norris in FP2. (Source: MEGA) Antonelli bounced back strongly in the second practice session for Mercedes, setting the fastest lap of the day with a 1:10.763 lap on the soft tyres, ahead of Norris. The 20-year-old finished 0.253 seconds ahead of Norris, who recorded a 1:11.016. Verstappen came third again in the day, just 0.006 seconds behind the McLaren driver. Russell briefly moved to second with a 1:11.036 before Norris and Verstappen improved their times. McLaren's Oscar Piastri finished fifth with a lap time of 1:11.084 seconds. View this post on Instagram Ferrari drivers endured a quiet start to the Brazil weekend. Hamilton took sixth after struggling to get tire temperatures up in the cooler track conditions. Charles Leclerc finished seventh after losing time when he had to veer toward the wall to avoid Haas debutant Rafael Câmara . Having already achieved his championship goal, Kimi Antonelli will now look to finish the season strongly and help his team secure the Constructors’ Championship. Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable for Sunday’s game with a rib injury, according to Detroit’s final injury report released Friday, Nov. 6. The wide receiver remained limited throughout the week, leaving Jared Goff’s offense waiting on a consequential availability decision. St. Brown has offered a more encouraging assessment.
